## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Lakkhaṇahāravibhaṅga* ("Conveying Characteristics: Analysis") is a section of the *Nettippakaraṇa* in the late canonical or paracanonical Pali literature [SuttaCentral]. It presents the detailed analysis (*vibhaṅga*) of the *lakkhaṇahāra*, one of the sixteen interpretive modes (*hāra*) formulated in the treatise for the exegesis of canonical discourses [SuttaCentral; Law 1923]. Bimala Charan Law notes that the historical foundation of the *Lakkhaṇahāra* in the *Nettippakaraṇa* can be traced to the venerable Mahākoṭṭhita's explanation regarding how wisdom (*paññā*) and discriminative consciousness (*viññāṇa*) are inseparably conjoined in reality (*ime dhammā saṃsaṭṭhā no visaṃsaṭṭhā*), an epistemological principle also reflected in the *Milindapañha* and the commentaries of Buddhaghosa [Law 1923].
Cross-references identified by SuttaCentral link the text to the corresponding fifth chapter of the *Peṭakopadesa* (*Hāravibhaṅgapañcamabhūmi*, Pe 5), as well as verses in the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 293), *Theragāthā* (Thag 13.1), Patna Dharmapada, and *Udānavarga*, alongside suttas in the *Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 47.3, SN 47.46) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse with 28 other texts, most heavily with the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* of the *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 6), the sub-commentary *Nettivibhāvinī*, the *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Uppādavāra* of the *Yamaka* (Ya 10.2.1), the *Samāropanahāravibhaṅga* (Ne 19), and Pe 5 [DharmaNexus]. Significant reuse is also documented with various Saṁyutta Nikāya collections—including SN 47, SN 45, SN 12, SN 22, and SN 35—and discourses in the Majjhima Nikāya (MN 38 and MN 149) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus records automated alignments with sections of the Tibetan *Śatasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā* and the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
